candidate.answerReason: Maria's day lasts 8 working hours plus 45 minutes for lunch. Starting at 7:25 A.M., she finishes at 4:10 P.M., matching choice C.

methods.label: Include the lunch break
methods.explanation:
The lunch break does not count toward Maria's \(8\) hours of work, so the time from starting to finishing is \(8\) hours \(45\) minutes.

Starting at \(7{:}25\) A.M., adding \(8\) hours brings us to \(3{:}25\) P.M. Adding the lunch break gives \(25+45=70\) minutes past \(3\). Since \(70\) minutes equals \(1\) hour \(10\) minutes, Maria finishes at \(\boxed{4{:}10\text{ P.M.}}\), choice C.
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary clock arithmetic and the conversion of 60 minutes to 1 hour.

candidate.annotationRationale: The assessed target is finding an ending clock time from a starting time and activity durations, including a separate break. No supplied catalog node explicitly covers this target, so it is proposed below. cnm_p063 covers finding a duration between two given times and is not assigned. The written method uses cnm_p062 to regroup 70 minutes as 1 hour 10 minutes; this is supporting knowledge for the task.

needsNewNodes.name: Finding an ending clock time
needsNewNodes.description: Determine an ending clock time from a starting time and one or more durations in hours and minutes. Include relevant breaks, regroup minutes across hour boundaries, and track A.M. and P.M.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog includes time-unit conversions and finding elapsed time between given endpoints, but neither explicitly covers calculating an unknown ending time.
